lesson.title: Skydiver Graphs and Formation Dive
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 1 Lesson 5: Skydiver Graphs and Formation Dive

gradingDesign.rule: All variable student evidence is graded only in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: In the scripted jump, what does the velocity-time graph show from 0 s to 4 s?
At what time does the scripted jump first reach terminal velocity? Enter the time in seconds.
What does the horizontal section of the velocity-time graph from 4 s to 10 s mean?
The velocity changes from 0 m/s to 45 m/s during the first 4 s. What is the average acceleration in m/s^2?
Why does the acceleration-time graph become negative after the parachute opens when downward is defined as positive?
When you change from Neutral or Spread to Dive, what should the acceleration graph show while speed approaches the faster Dive terminal velocity?
Why does the acceleration graph move below zero when you change from Dive to Spread?
After the partner deploys a parachute, the partner appears to rise in the tracking camera. Which explanation is correct?
Describe one body-position change from your formation dive. Cite the before-and-after motion or graph evidence and explain how the change affected your speed or altitude gap relative to the partner.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Use a specific Dive, Neutral, or Spread change and evidence from your run.
a. Full credit: Identifies a body-position change, cites a relevant readout or graph change, and accurately explains its effect on speed or relative altitude gap.
  Partial credit: Describes a reasonable position change but gives vague evidence or an incomplete connection to relative motion.
  No credit: Gives no identifiable trial event, claims body position has no effect, or contradicts the displayed evidence.

questions.prompt: Explain your formation-dive strategy using body position, parachute timing, and evidence from both the velocity-time and acceleration-time graphs. Include how the partner can appear to move upward even while still falling.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Cite your own run and connect body position, deployment, both graph types, and relative motion.
a. Full credit: Explains how body position changed drag and terminal velocity, explains how parachute timing produced a large acceleration opposite the downward motion, cites features from both graphs, and correctly explains the partner's apparent upward motion as relative motion.
  Partial credit: Gives a sound strategy and some graph evidence but omits one graph, deployment timing, or the relative-motion explanation.
  No credit: Gives no usable strategy, treats negative acceleration as upward velocity, or says the partner actually flies upward after deployment.
